_raw.permit_cost: $6 reservation fee + $8 per person per night
_raw.special_requirements: Bear canisters required; designated campsites only in high-use areas
_raw.permit_pickup_location: Olympic National Park Wilderness Information Center, Port Angeles, WA
_raw.seasonal_closure_dates: High-use overnight camping May 1 - Sept 30 (reservation-only); closed to overnight access other times based on snow conditions

access.fees: None beyond the trailhead parking pass this route already lists.
access.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the trailhead parking pass and wilderness camping permit apply.
access.rules: Group size capped at 12 people / 8 stock; groups of 7+ must use designated Group Sites. Bear-resistant food containers mandatory park-wide for overnight trips — free loaners at Wilderness Information Centers.
access.closures: High-use overnight camping May 1 - Sept 30 (reservation-only); closed to overnight access other times based on snow conditions
access.land_manager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency Pass or Scan & Pay at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead — $5 per vehicle per day or $30 annual. The trailhead is on Olympic National Forest land (Quilcene Ranger District), so no Olympic National Park entrance fee is charged to park there.

overnight_permit.what: Olympic National Park wilderness permit — quota at Royal Lake, not free
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov; the Royal Lake quota sells out quickly. Bear canisters are required in Royal Basin.

access.fees: USFS trailhead day-use fee $5/vehicle/day or $30/year (Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency 'America the Beautiful' pass accepted in lieu of the day fee), plus the $6 NPS wilderness-permit reservation fee for overnight trips.
access.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the trailhead parking pass and wilderness camping permit apply.
access.rules: Bear canisters are mandatory for food storage in Royal Basin. Camping is restricted to three designated areas: Royal Creek, Lower Royal Meadow, and Royal Lake; groups of 7 or more must use designated group campsites.
access.permit: NPS wilderness permit required for any overnight stay in Royal Basin/upper mountain, reserved via recreation.gov ($6 non-refundable reservation fee); online reservations for the May 15-Oct 15 season typically open around mid-April; camp areas are quota-limited.
access.landManager: Trailhead and lower approach trail (Upper Dungeness Trail #833, Royal Basin Trail #832 to the wilderness boundary) are on Olympic National Forest, Hood Canal Ranger District; the upper basin and the peak itself are within Olympic National Park's Daniel J. Evans Wilderness.
